doc.title: Peter Appleyard interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 4, 2012

title: Hosting Goodman in Toronto, Ames Iowa concert, cufflinks and negotiating pay
summary: After hosting Goodman, Appleyard played Ames with the Philharmonic, received cufflinks, and negotiated pay equal to Zoot Sims.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: And Benny playing the Weber Clarinet Concerto, with seven thousand people waiting to hear “Honeysuckle Rose.” It was incredible. So after we finished that night he said, “Let’s go and get something to eat.” So I said, “Okay.” So we went off to get something to eat and I was having some apple pie. So he reached over and he said, “Let me try a piece of that.” So he took — “oh that’s good,” he said, “oh by the way this is for you.” And it was a jewelry box. I said, “What’s this for, Benny?” He said, “That’s for your hospitality in Toronto. Open it.” I opened it and it was a pair of hand-sculpted nugget solid gold cufflinks, which I had appraised recently and the guy said, at Tiffany’s, and he said, today, three or four thousand dollars. Ask him for a raise and he’d go insane. He’d go insane. We were going to Europe and I was in the apartment and he was paying me, I forget whether it was five hundred for the week or something. Of course this was in 1973 or ’74. And we were to do five concerts you know.
